name: Dust pressing
summary: Nearly dry clay powder is pressed in a steel die under high pressure to form a tile in one step. The tile needs little drying and keeps its size.
how: Grind the clay and sieve it to a fine powder with about 6 per cent water.
Fill the steel die and press the powder under a screw or hydraulic press.
Remove the tile and fire it with no long drying.
Keep the size of each tile within 0.5 mm.

origin.note: Richard Prosser takes out a patent for pressing tiles from clay dust, and Minton uses it for floor tiles.

adoptions.via: Minton and other Staffordshire firms press floor tiles from dust in a steel die, and the tiles have square, even edges.
New York tile works press small white wall tiles from dust, with bevelled edges and ribs on the back.
